record.original_question:
Describe all n×n Rayleigh matrices, meaning P-matrices A for which the
polynomial f_A(z)=det(A+diag(z1,...,zn)) is a
Rayleigh polynomial.

evidence.quote: Problem 44 (Rayleigh matrices, [13]). Describe all n × n Rayleigh matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real n×n matrix A is called a P-matrix if every principal minor of A is positive. Given an n×n matrix A, define the polynomial
  f_A(z_1,...,z_n) = det(A + diag(z_1,...,z_n)) ∈ ℝ[z_1,...,z_n].
A multiaffine polynomial p(z_1,...,z_n) with positive coefficients is said to be Rayleigh if for every pair of indices i ≠ j and every point x = (x_1,...,x_n) with x_k > 0 for all k, the Rayleigh inequality
  (∂p/∂z_i)(x) · (∂p/∂z_j)(x) ≥ p(x) · (∂²p/∂z_i ∂z_j)(x)
holds. Call an n×n P-matrix A a Rayleigh matrix if the polynomial f_A(z_1,...,z_n) is a Rayleigh polynomial. Describe (classify) all n×n Rayleigh matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying Rayleigh matrices arises from the Choe–Wagner theory of Rayleigh matroids and related negative-dependence work by Borcea–Brändén–Liggett. While Rayleigh matroids have been characterized in the binary case (no S_8 minor) and strongly Rayleigh measures have been heavily studied, no complete description of all n×n Rayleigh matrices in the sense above appears in the literature, and the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Rayleigh Matroids (Choe–Wagner)
status_evidence.snippet: Rayleigh matroids were introduced, motivated by linear resistive electrical networks; binary matroids are Rayleigh iff they do not contain S_8 as a minor.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification exists for the matroidal analogue, but the matrix-level classification is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Negative dependence and the geometry of polynomials (Borcea–Brändén–Liggett)
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly Rayleigh measures defined via stability of generating polynomials; class includes determinantal and spanning tree measures.
status_evidence.claim: The Rayleigh property has been studied extensively but no complete description of Rayleigh matrices is given.
